info.name: CanTrack — Walker Glass
info.description: The eight new walker/owner endpoints (raise, favourites, walk summary, availability, dog note, weekly goal, walking route): Happy path then Exploits then Cleanup; every exploit must get the 4xx in its name. Environment: baseUrl, ownerToken, ownerId, otherOwnerToken, otherOwnerId, walkerToken, walkerId, dogId (a dog owned by the owner). Run top to bottom: the happy path builds the data the exploits and cleanup need (walk online -> open request -> raise -> accept -> pick -> assigned walk), the exploits only reject, and the cleanup unfavourites, clears the note, cancels the request and restores availability/goal.

request.description: Baseline for the online switch: the later cleanup restores exactly the state the walker had before the collection ran.
Going online upserts the heartbeat row (walker_positions) and needs bounded coordinates. The walker must be online with a fresh heartbeat for the offer on the request below to be allowed.

item.name: Owner posts a walk request (setup for raise and pick)

request.description: The owner opens a request for their own dog five days ahead, next to the walker's position (inside the 2 km bidding radius). This request is what the walker accepts and the owner picks, which makes the walker one of the owner's clients; the cleanup cancels it.

item.name: Owner posts a second request for the raise tests

request.description: Raise only works while a request is open, and the first request gets picked below, so this second open request is what the raise happy path and its exploits use; the cleanup cancels it.
Only the owning owner, only while open, only upwards: 20000 -> 22000 and the offer window restarts.

item.name: Walker accepts the fare (setup for pick)

request.description: An accept takes the owner's fare (the first request is still at 20000; the raise went to the second request). Setup for the pick that makes the walker one of the owner's clients.
The assigned walk is what turns the owner into the walker's client and the walker into a walker the owner can favourite.

exec: pm.test("the owner is a client", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().some(function (c) { return c.ownerId === pm.environment.get("ownerId"); })).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Baseline read that captures the walker's existing private note on the dog, so the cleanup can put back exactly what was there.

exec: pm.test("dog listed", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().dogs.some(function (d) { return d.id === pm.environment.get("dogId"); })).to.eql(true); });
const dog = pm.response.json().dogs.find(function (d) { return d.id === pm.environment.get("dogId"); }); pm.environment.set("noteBaseline", dog && dog.note ? dog.note : "");

request.description: Baseline read for the weekly goal (the earnings answer carries goalCop), so the cleanup can restore the value the walker had.

exec: pm.test("month totals", function () { const b = pm.response.json().month; pm.expect(b).to.have.property("walks"); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("km"); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("minutes"); });
pm.test("tab counts", function () { const c = pm.response.json().counts; pm.expect(c).to.have.property("upcoming"); pm.expect(c).to.have.property("active"); pm.expect(c).to.have.property("past"); });
pm.test("the assigned walk counts as upcoming", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().counts.upcoming).to.be.at.least(1); });

request.description: Works here because the walker took one of the owner's walks (the pick above); the exploits folder shows the 404 for a stranger.

exec: pm.test("walker is a favourite", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().walkers.some(function (w) { return w.walkerId === pm.environment.get("walkerId") && w.favorite === true; })).to.eql(true); });

item.name: Walker writes a private note on the dog

body.raw: {"note": "Firulais: el portero no abre antes de las 7."}

request.description: The dog is one the walker walked (the assigned request), so the note is accepted; no owner ever reads it back.

exec: pm.test("note stored", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().note).to.eql("Firulais: el portero no abre antes de las 7."); });

request.description: Walker's pin to the owner's home pin, both inside Pasto. A routing failure answers 200 with source straight, never an error.
IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the owner's request id. _owned_request answers 403 before any state changes.

exec: pm.test("not your walk", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Not your walk request."); });

request.description: 22000 is the fare after the happy-path raise on the still-open second request, and only an upwards change is allowed.
priceCop must be between 0 and 1000000; the validation handler answers every rejected body with a 400.
IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the owner's id; owner_from_path refuses before any query.

exec: pm.test("own account only", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("your own account"); });

item.name: Favourite a walker who never walked → 404

request.description: Happy path is impossible for a stranger: only a walker who already took one of the owner's walks can be marked, so the documented 404 (UNKNOWN_WALKER_MESSAGE) is asserted instead. otherOwnerId is a real account that never walked for the owner.

exec: pm.test("walker not found", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Walker not found."); });

request.description: favorite must be a boolean and Pydantic does not coerce this string; the validation handler answers 400.
IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the owner's id.
Role check: the walker token against the owner's id is refused before any query.
IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the walker's id; walker_from_path refuses an owner before any query.
Going online needs bounded coordinates; the switch without them is a 400 and leaves the walker offline.

exec: pm.test("location message", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("lat must be between"); });

item.name: Another owner writes the walker's note → 403

request.description: IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the walker's id.

item.name: Note on a dog the walker never walked → 404

request.description: A dog counts as the walker's client's only when one of his own walks with that owner was for it; an unknown dog id gets the documented 404.

exec: pm.test("not their clients dog", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("Not one of your clients"); });

request.description: The note is capped at 500 characters (MAX_NOTE_LENGTH); the validation handler answers 400.
IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the walker's id.
goalCop must be between 10000 and 5000000 COP.

item.name: Another owner asks for the route → 403

request.description: IDOR: otherOwnerToken against the walker's id.
Both points must be inside Pasto; the endpoint takes no body, so this query pair is its bad-input 400.

exec: pm.test("favourite removed", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().walkers.some(function (w) { return w.walkerId === pm.environment.get("walkerId") && w.favorite === true; })).to.eql(false); });

request.description: Puts back the note captured in the client-detail read (null clears). Runs before the cancel below, while the walk is still assigned and the dog is still the walker's client's.

exec: const base = pm.environment.get("noteBaseline"); pm.environment.set("noteRestoreBody", base ? JSON.stringify({ note: base }) : JSON.stringify({ note: null }));
pm.test("note back to baseline", function () { const base = pm.environment.get("noteBaseline"); const now = pm.response.json().note; pm.expect(now === (base || null)).to.eql(true); });

item.name: Owner cancels the still-open raise request

request.description: Undoes the second request the raise tests used (open -> cancelled).

item.name: Owner cancels the assigned walk request

request.description: Undoes the assigned walk the happy path created (assigned -> cancelled).
Restores the online/offline state read at the start of the run.

exec: if (pm.environment.get("availabilityWasOnline") === true) { pm.environment.set("availabilityRestoreBody", JSON.stringify({ online: true, lat: 1.2076, lng: -77.2768 })); } else { pm.environment.set("availabilityRestoreBody", JSON.stringify({ online: false })); }

request.description: Puts back the goal captured in the earnings read. When the walker had no goal the API has no unset, so the minimum (10000) is stored and the change stays bounded.

exec: const base = pm.environment.get("goalBaseline"); pm.environment.set("goalRestoreBody", JSON.stringify({ goalCop: base ? Number(base) : 10000 }));
pm.test("back to baseline", function () { const base = pm.environment.get("goalBaseline"); pm.expect(pm.response.json().goalCop).to.eql(base ? Number(base) : 10000); });
